runs.summary: T-070 is still on hold: I logged that the centre's Dodo webhook from T-122 is now live and only needs Dodo's endpoint and its signing secret, but Bharath still has to say what api.usetantra.com does with these payments. I acked note R-e9193f50 and committed the change.

decisions.why: Adi put this on hold himself on 2026-09-24 ('integrated later'). T-122 is done: the centre's own Dodo endpoint grants seat and VIP access. No local repo holds the api.usetantra.com backend code, and the test purchase waits on T-005, the last task after launch.

decisions.decision: Do the read-only half now. Do not change tantra-backend-v2. In the T-070 log, record what the local code at Documents/GitHub/tantra-backend-v2/src/domains/billing/webhooks/billing-webhook.processor.ts does with a workshop payment for pdt_0NnpA6EIxXvDvS1F03N8Z. It is a one-time payment.* event, so onPayment() (lines 102-108) stores a payment row and answers 200. If the buyer's email matches no Tantra user, the outcome is 'unmatched'. Either way it grants no plan, because only subscription.* events in the catalog reach applySubscription. Stripe payments (T-218) never reach it. Conclusion: the Tantra Plan has to be granted from the centre's attendee list (T-122, done), later through the backend's existing BillingTrialCampaignService.grant. Write that as the integration plan. Ask Bharath on the task to confirm prod runs this code. In the app repo, change 'Build Pass' to '$99 seat / VIP' in checkout/route.ts line 5 and dodo/webhook/route.ts line 83, then run tsc, commit and push. Leave the task on hold.
decisions.why: The backend code is local and can be read, so the 'what does it do' question gets answered now. The owner's hold (2026-09-24) covers integration only. two-funnel-structure bans the Build Pass name. T-122 already grants access from the centre.
